text: The first tape box shall play a household member's recording of a book when a card is put on it, built from wave-1 parts only, powered over USB, with no radio but the NFC reader.
rationale: The household builds the smallest box that does the nightly job, uses it, and lets use decide what comes next. Card watcher and enclosure leaves are Modulo's (TAPE-CARD, TAPE-ENC) and are adopted unchanged, not repeated here.

text: The scope of the first box shall stay at wave-1 parts and no WiFi or Bluetooth.
rationale: Cutting WiFi removes the ingest server, the captive portal, every /api route, the radio state rule and the attack Morphyx found. That's what it's worth. What it costs is that copying to the SD by hand is clumsier, and that cost is measured in TAPE1-USE.

text: The first parts order shall contain no part whose wave in parts.json is 2.
acceptance: A-BOM: proposals/mozzie-cut.mjs part 1 prints the wave-1 total in both tiers ($50 unbranded / $102 as linked on today's parts.json), and the order list compared to it has zero wave-2 ids.
rationale: Tape already splits its order into waves. Wave 2 (charger, cell, boost) is what the read-range answer might change. A box on a bedside table can use a phone charger.

text: The firmware image shall not initialise the WiFi or Bluetooth stacks.
acceptance: I-RADIO: sdkconfig has CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_ENABLED and CONFIG_BT_ENABLED unset, and the des model has no state that raises a radio.
rationale: If the radio is never up, then nothing on the network can reach the recordings, and a false card-gone costs a pause and nothing more.

text: The box shall treat the microSD card as the only way in for audio and the only record of which card plays what.
rationale: Without a network, the SD is the interface, so its rules are the product's rules.

text: At boot the box shall treat each folder under /tape/audio whose name matches tape's title-id rule as one title, playing its decodable files in name order whatever their extension.
acceptance: T-FOLDER: a simulated SD holding .m4a, .mp3 and .opus files, plus one badly named folder, gives the expected titles and track order, and the bad folder is listed in /tape/log.txt and not played.
rationale: A voice memo copied straight from the phone has to work. tape's catalog.js requires 000.opus names and stored durations, which only the studio writes. v1 doesn't use that part of it.

text: When a card with no binding is placed and an unbound folder exists, the box shall bind the card to the first unbound folder in name order and start playing it.
acceptance: T-BIND: in the des model, 1000 scripted placements match the rule. Binding happens only on placement, never on boot.
rationale: This replaces ENROLLING, the 60 s window and /api/enroll. The card in your hand when you first hear the book is the book's card.

text: The box shall never change an existing card binding and shall never write, rename or delete anything under /tape/audio.
acceptance: T-KEEP: 200 simulated household months (proposals/mozzie-cut.mjs) show 0 violations of P1 or P2, and the mutant bind-any is caught (it fails 159/200 today).
rationale: Morphyx's keeper rule, met by construction. Only a person with the SD in a computer can re-point or remove a recording.

text: After a power cut at any step of saving a binding, the box shall boot with either the previous bindings or the new ones.
acceptance: T-CUT: the power is cut at every SD step of one bind and at random steps across 200 months, with 0 failures. The mutant in-place (cards.json written directly) is caught by both.
rationale: A child pulls the plug. A torn cards.json that reads as empty would let every card re-bind to new folders, which breaks KEEP by a different route.

text: When a card with no binding is placed and no unbound folder exists, the box shall play a short cue and append the card's id to /tape/unknown.txt.
acceptance: T-UNKNOWN: in the des model, the cue event is emitted, the line is appended, and the card stays unbound.
rationale: Silence reads as broken. The file gives a grown-up the id of a card to re-point by hand.

text: The box shall identify a card by its tape NDEF pointer when lib/tag.js decodes one, and otherwise by the tag's UID.
acceptance: T-ID: a written tag, a blank NTAG213 and a tag with a corrupt record each give the expected id.
rationale: Factory-blank stickers work on day one with no tag writing. Cards written later by Web NFC still work, so the pointer design stays open.

text: The box shall append one line to /tape/log.txt for each boot, each binding and each finished title.
acceptance: T-USELOG: in the des model, a scripted month gives the expected line counts, and a boot after a folder was added is marked as an SD change.
rationale: Use is the evidence. After a month this log says whether copying to the SD by hand was a chore (many SD changes, grumbling) or rare. That evidence, not a guess, is what decides whether WiFi ingest (tape's wave 3) is built.

text: The enclosure shall let a grown-up remove and reinsert the microSD card without tools and without opening the case, and shall not let a child reach it by accident.
acceptance: I-SD: on the printed box, someone who didn't build it swaps the card in under 30 s, and the slot is on the underside or the back.
rationale: If the SD is the only way in, a slot that needs a screwdriver turns every new book into a project.

text: A household member who did not build the box shall record a book, copy it to the SD, bind a card and hear it played to the end.
acceptance: D-HOUSE: done once, start to finish, with no help from the builder, using only the phone's voice-memo app and whatever computer or SD adapter the house already owns.
rationale: This is the whole point. If it needs the builder standing by, the job isn't done.
